record.title: Preprint reports data-composition scaling laws for synthetic tool-use agent training
record.summary: An Apple-affiliated preprint introduces SynthAPI, a pipeline that generates executable tool-use environments with configurable diversity across tools, tasks and database states. The authors report experiments spanning 458,752 tasks and 849 Qwen3.5 models, and a composition-aware scaling law with lower held-out error than a task-count-only fit. They also report benchmark gains over selected prior methods, while noting that some comparisons use different training regimes. The study is confined to synthetic, research-only simulations; its authors say transfer beyond this single synthesis pipeline is not established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: An Apple-affiliated author team submitted arXiv preprint 2610.37648v1 on October 27, 2026, describing SynthAPI, a pipeline for generating executable synthetic tool-use environments.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report varying task and environment composition across 458,752 generated tasks and 849 trained models in four Qwen3.5 sizes. Their proposed composition-aware scaling law predicts held-out downstream scores with mean absolute error 0.0285 on the top 25% of training-FLOP runs, compared with 0.1706 for a task-count-only fit.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that SynthAPI-Big exceeds SimSAT on AppWorld Test-Challenge by 7.6 percentage points for the 4B model and 11.6 points for the 9B model, and exceeds the strongest listed BFCL baseline by 2.0 points at 4B and 3.7 points at 8B. The paper notes that the BFCL methods use substantially different training regimes, so those comparisons do not isolate synthesis-method effects or data efficiency.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that its scaling relationship transfers to other synthetic-data pipelines, training settings, deployed agents, or production workflows; the authors say it is validated on one pipeline and report experiments only in research-only simulated environments.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of SynthAPI generation, the fitted scaling relationship or reported benchmark results was located or performed.
Transfer to different synthetic environment pipelines, training methods and realistic user-in-the-loop workflows is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported composition effects and predictive scaling relationship replicate, they could change how substantial tool-use agent training budgets are allocated across task, tool, and state diversity. The work is notable for training-data and evaluation choices, while evidence remains one paper on one synthetic pipeline and research-only simulations.
limitations: All reported results are from one author-reported preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The proposed scaling relationship is validated on a single data-synthesis pipeline; the authors state transfer to other pipelines or training settings is not guaranteed.
Tasks do not include a user in the loop, and the generated content lacks the semantic depth of long realistic documents such as email chains or notes.
All tool-use experiments use research-only simulated environments and do not establish deployed-product or production-workflow outcomes.
Benchmark comparisons use different model families, datasets and training regimes; the authors state these comparisons do not isolate the synthesis method or relative data efficiency.
The arXiv landing page exposed no linked code or dataset during this review, so generated tasks, model checkpoints, benchmark outputs and analysis were not independently inspected or rerun.
brief.summary: An Apple-affiliated preprint introduces SynthAPI, a pipeline that generates executable tool-use environments with configurable diversity across tools, tasks and database states. The authors report experiments spanning 458,752 tasks and 849 Qwen3.5 models, and a composition-aware scaling law with lower held-out error than a task-count-only fit. They also report benchmark gains over selected prior methods, while noting that some comparisons use different training regimes. The study is confined to synthetic, research-only simulations; its authors say transfer beyond this single synthesis pipeline is not established.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that data composition improves prediction of downstream scores and that higher training budgets benefit from more tool/app diversity, more database profiles per task and more complex database states. Their selected recipe also scores above listed baselines on several benchmark comparisons.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv v1 contains the method, experiment description, reported measurements and stated limitations. This review did not independently reproduce any result.
technical.mechanism: SynthAPI uses a language model to generate executable Python apps backed by structured databases, then creates tasks with verifiers, starting states and solver programs. The experiments vary app/tool count, tasks per app, initial database profiles and distractor-data complexity. GLM-5.2 generated expert trajectories for SFT of Qwen3.5 student models.
technical.regime: 458,752 generated tasks across 64 apps; 849 trained models in four Qwen3.5 sizes; held-out extrapolation with the top 25% of training-FLOP runs excluded from fit; evaluations include AppWorld, BFCLv3 multi-turn, ASTRA-Bench and a SynthAPI holdout. The environments are synthetic and research-only.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the scaling-law fit, a task-count-only curve is the direct reported baseline. For selected benchmark comparisons, the paper compares against SimSAT on AppWorld and EnvFactory/EnvScaler on BFCL; methods use different datasets and, for BFCL, different SFT/RL training regimes.

brief.title: Preprint reports data-composition scaling laws for synthetic tool-use agent training
brief.why_it_matters: Agent-training budgets are often described by how many trajectories or tasks they contain. If the reported results replicate, composition across tools and database states may be a consequential training-design variable, and the proposed fit could help allocate data budgets. The paper does not show that its gains transfer beyond the tested pipeline or simulated tasks.
